summary: In this fiction excerpt, Chloe asks Marcel about Arthur's old bookshop, and Arthur explains it was never really a bookshop: the aim was to put books in everyday places so people fall in love with reading. He describes having local kids curate anthologies from The Story So Far, matching the right book to the right person in the right place. Chloe then gives Arthur a carefully wrapped birthday book, which the children gather to watch him unwrap, before the scene shifts into a surreal passage.
one_line: Arthur explains his unconventional bookshop strategy of placing books where kids already are, while Chloe celebrates his birthday with a homemade book.
key_facts: Arthur says his project 'wasn't a bookshop' because bookshops were practically the only place to get a book back then.
Arthur argues that books must be everywhere, in places people go before they know they are readers.
Arthur says the secret was connecting kids with their local neighborhoods and the tastes there.
The kids curated their own anthologies of the best, most suitable material from The Story So Far.
Arthur says: 'The right book for the right person in the right place.'
Arthur compares the approach to giving someone a religious experience before luring them into church regularly.
Chloe says it is Arthur's birthday and calls him 'you old sod'.
Chloe introduces Marcel to Arthur, and they shake hands.
Chloe gives Arthur a carefully wrapped package containing a book he is delighted to receive.
The wrapped book has a nylon cover from an old backpack, worn denim, and an embroidered title on the spine.
Arthur says 'You didn't' and Chloe replies 'I certainly did'.
Arthur moves on his exoskeleton, which has oiled, carefully balanced carapace.
The excerpt ends with a reference to 'Better than Great Expectations again' and a voice saying 'The Story So Far'.
